History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old man with known asthma presents via tele-consult with 3-hour history of chest tightness, mild exertional dyspnea, wheeze, and non-productive cough after 1-week lapse in both rescue and controller inhalers.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset chest “tightness” today (~3 h duration).  
• Associated symptoms: mild shortness of breath (worse on stairs, not at rest), wheeze, dry cough. No frank chest pain, hemoptysis, or fever reported.  
• Recent illness: Viral URI last week with sore throat and runny nose (now improving); persistent cough.  
• Triggers/relief: No inhaler use for one week (ran out while at university). No other relieving measures tried.  
• Severity/progression: First episode of this severity since adolescence; concerned about repeat intubation.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives/positives limited to above).

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – childhood onset; severe exacerbation age 16–17 necessitating intubation; previously well-controlled on beclomethasone (Clenil) + Salbutamol.  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.  
• Childhood eczema (resolved).  
• Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).

Medications:
• Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; out of supply x1 week.  
• Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; out of supply x1 week.  
• No current oral medications.  
Allergies: Denies drug allergies; environmental allergy to dust.

Social History:
• University student; currently away at school.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: not discussed (missing).

Family History:
• Father – asthma.  
• Mother – eczema.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded (tele-consult).  
General/Respiratory: Speaking full sentences; reports no dyspnea at rest. No further exam performed.

Investigations:
None ordered or performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Likely mild–moderate acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by recent viral URI and one-week lapse in inhaler therapy.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute asthma exacerbation – strong history of asthma, recent medication lapse, wheeze/tightness, viral trigger.  
2. Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airway – lingering cough after URI; less likely given longstanding asthma.  
3. Community-acquired pneumonia – low likelihood; afebrile, non-productive cough, no focal signs.

Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation
• Prescription: 
  – Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler (dose not documented).  
  – Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler (dose not documented) for maintenance.  
  – Oral corticosteroid burst (prednisolone; exact dose not documented) 2 tablets each morning for 5 days.  
  – Spacer device with instruction leaflet.  
• Education: Use Ventolin PRN; if requires >1 puff every 3 h, seek medical care. Resume Clenil twice daily once acute symptoms settle (exact regimen to be provided on label). Spacer technique reviewed.  
• Safety-net: Attend ED/seek urgent care for worsening SOB, chest tightness, dizziness, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Follow-up: Arrange review if no improvement after steroid course or sooner if deteriorates.

Issue 2: Medication supply / adherence
• Action: Ensure timely pharmacy collection; advise setting reminders and keeping spare inhalers at university.  
• Plan: Add repeat prescriptions for both inhalers; consider written asthma action plan at next review.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis / hay fever
• Current status not troublesome; no treatment requested.  
• Plan: Re-address if nasal or ocular symptoms recur.

General plan items:
• Rest from work/studies until feeling better (self-certify first 7 days).  
• Encourage peak-flow monitoring in future; provide device at next in-person visit.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: vitals, objective lung exam, smoking/alcohol history, exact medication doses.  
• No contradictions between transcript and DDx identified.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; brief audio dropout during steroid discussion noted.
